messages:
Sam: Heads up — CI perf job on release/candidate-3.4 flagged a p99 token latency regression ~1.8x for the kernel selection path. Rollout is blocked until we root cause. :eyes:
CI-bot: perf/latency-nightly job failed: p99_tokens increased from 22ms -> 39ms on runtime-kernel-select tests (see logs). https://ci.internal/redwood/jobs/8742 :warning:
Jess: ack. I saw an alert earlier. Saw similar spike on canary yesterday but thought it was noise. Which test suite is failing exactly?
Sam: It's the small-seq workload (seq_len distribution skewed to 512-1500). Kernel selector is choosing fallback kernel more often. Failing test: runtime/kernels/select_perf:batching+kv-on.
Marta: Repro attempt locally with the nightly image — I can repro p99 jump when kv cache hit ratio drops below ~12%. Profiling shows extra memcpy and a kernel fallback path. Paste of perf summary: ```
# perf top sample
  25.4%  runtime.so  kernel_selector::choose
  18.1%  runtime.so  kv::evict_and_fetch
  12.0%  runtime.so  fallback_kernels::attention_loop
```
Andre: Interesting. Any recent commits touching the selector heuristics or KV eviction? I'll start a git bisect.
Sam: I traced to a merge from feature/batching-heuristics last night but not 100% sure. The merge includes two PRs: one that changes `ssel_pref_threshold` and another that tweaks kv eviction batch size.
Jess: Proposed bisect commands: ```
git checkout release/candidate-3.4
git bisect start HEAD <good-commit-sha>
git bisect run ./tools/perf_repro.sh --suite kernels/select_perf
```
Marta: I ran `perf_repro.sh` locally but it takes ~6m per run — should we narrow to a faster smoke that triggers the kernel switch? Maybe reproduce with `SEQ_DIST=heavy-512-1500 ./tools/smoke_kselect.sh` to speed up.
Andre: Starting bisect with smoke script now and will post the suspect commit when found. Will run parallel on my machine and CI.
CI-bot: Queued bisect job on ci-runner-7 (using smoke script). Output will be posted in thread.
(25m later)
Andre: Found first bad commit: a4c9b2f — "heuristics: prefer fallback kernel when average_seq>512" — makes selector favor fallback for mid-long sequences. When combined with kv eviction changes, fallback path hits memcpy hotspots.
Jess: Can you paste `git show` for a4c9b2f?
Andre: ```
git show --name-only a4c9b2f
commit a4c9b2f
Author: Priya <priya@redwood.com>
Date:   Thu Mar 12 03:40:11 2026 -0700

    heuristics: prefer fallback kernel when average_seq>512

 runtime/selector.rs
 runtime/kv_cache.rs
```
Marta: So it's not just selector; the same merge also updated `kv_cache.rs` to increase eviction aggressiveness (batch threshold 0.15 -> 0.10). Combo effect reduces warm cache hits and pushes requests down fallback path more often.
Sam: That matches my local profile. Plan options: 1) revert a4c9b2f as hotfix 2) tweak heuristics to be less aggressive (prefer baseline kernel unless hit ratio < X) 3) tune kv eviction back. Which is fastest?
Jess: For rollout unblock, revert a4c9b2f in candidate branch and run canary. If revert causes other regressions, do quick A/B with adjusted thresholds.
Andre: I'll open a revert PR and include the bisect logs + perf snapshots. Assigning to Priya for follow-up on a proper fix. PR: https://git.redwood/reverts/revert-a4c9b2f
Sam: Thanks. Marta/Jess — can you validate canary after revert? I can run the perf job.
Marta: Will run smoke and the full kernel select perf suite once revert lands. ETA ~30m.
(40m later)
deploy-bot: deploy/candidate-3.4 reverted commit a4c9b2f -> canary started.
Marta: Canary results: p99 back to baseline 23ms on runtime-kernel-select. KV hit ratio restored. :thumbsup:
Jess: Great. Leaving rollout unblocked. Follow-up: Priya to propose safer guardrails (unit test for selector, explicit interaction test with kv eviction) and add perf regression alerts on PRs that touch both modules.
Andre: I'll add a tiny e2e that simulates mid-long seq distribution and assert kernel selection distribution doesn't degrade more than 10%.
Sam: Thanks all. Filing postmortem link and tagging owners. Priya please chime in here about the intended benefit of the heuristic so we can preserve it safely. :shipit:
